episode.title: Prevent context-budget collapse for DeepSeek's canonical flash alias

evidence_units.claim: Issue #11894 reports that the official DeepSeek endpoint accepts `deepseek-flash` and `deepseek-v4-pro`, rejects the DashScope spelling `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, and that direct `deepseek-flash` resolution produces 131072 input and 32000 output; measured long `/review --effort high` sessions repeatedly compacted and one died with `COMPRESSION_FAILED_OUTPUT_TRUNCATED`, while a 1,000,000 context workaround completed normally.

The parent implementation table is first-match ordered: `/^deepseek-v4/` maps input to the 1,000,000 bucket before `/^deepseek/` maps other DeepSeek names to 131072; the output table has `/^deepseek-v4/` at 384000 but no generic DeepSeek output row, leaving unmatched names to the 32000 default.

The pinned implementation widens both existing V4 rows to `/^deepseek-(?:v4|flash)/`, keeps the input row before the generic `/^deepseek/` fallback and the output row before the older-family rows, and documents the official-versus-DashScope spelling distinction.

Commit `3987391392611e5d1f66851681f13ee7e55f4864` has parent `156092e892db5b098bd6d0ecf606dd37449538fe`, changes two files, and reports 12 additions and 2 deletions: the core limit table and its test.

The head test adds a dedicated case asserting `tokenLimit('deepseek-flash')` equals 1000000 and `tokenLimit('deepseek-flash', 'output')` equals 384000, alongside the existing V4 and older-family cases.

The input call site in `modelConfigResolver.ts` uses `knownTokenLimit(modelId, 'input')` to auto-fill `contextWindowSize` when no explicit provider value exists, which is the custom-provider path implicated by the issue.

The OpenAI-compatible default provider and Anthropic generator call `tokenLimit(model, 'output')` together with `hasExplicitOutputLimit`, so widening the output row changes the alias from unknown-model handling to the existing known-V4 output-budget path.

The PR test plan reports a direct probe of 1000000 input and 384000 output for `deepseek-flash`, unchanged neighboring values, and `vitest run src/core/tokenLimits.test.ts` passing 91/91; it also states that reverting the regex makes the new case fail at 131072/32000.

A PR verification comment reports a two-tree CLI `/context` A/B: `deepseek-flash` is 1000.0k on the head and 131.1k with the merge-base table, while `deepseek-xyz` remains 131.1k as a control; the context/compaction ladder moves with the corrected window and the relevant product CI lanes are green.

A maintainer's real-build verification isolates the two regex rows, reports 91/91 unit tests at head and exactly one reverted-test failure, measures `deepseek-flash` changing from 131072/32000/unknown/32000 to 1000000/384000/known/64000, shows a 250k prompt is safe after the change rather than entering compaction, and reproduces then removes the reported compression failure using an injected prompt count.

Review verification records that bare `deepseek-v4` remains 131.1k in both trees because `normalize()` strips a trailing `-v4` before table matching; this is pre-existing and not fixed by the pinned change.

The maintainer verification records that the VS Code companion contains a duplicated, unsynchronized table with no production importer, and that the built-in provider preset may have a separate endpoint-name issue even though its explicit context setting avoids this auto-bucketing failure; both are outside the pinned core diff.

The review identifies the narrow solution boundary: widen the two existing table rows rather than rewrite the shared normalizer or modify only a provider preset, and preserve the specific older DeepSeek rows and generic fallback ordering.
